# Introduction

Autotuning is already a game — it is simply played by hand.  A kernel
engineer looks at a spelled program, chooses fusions and strength
reductions, picks a schedule, compiles, measures, and iterates; the
moves are well-formed, the referee is the numeric check, and the score
is wall time.  What the incumbent toolchains automate is the *scoring*
(a cost model over a template space); the *move set* stays whatever a
human wrote into the compiler.

The mlopt substrate [@mlopt-platform] supplies the rest of the game as
machinery: a term IR and an e-graph that closes a program under a law
bank, a certificate that replays a derivation step-by-step, a `Sink`
port that lowers an extracted program into a backend and verifies it,
and a game layer — the `Board` protocol, the episode/train/eval
drivers, and the player registry — that already plays law discovery
on the same primitives [@mlopt-graphopt].  kernelopt is the domain
package that seats codegen on that layer: one spelled program, a law
bank of codegen rewrites as the move set, a launch-dominated cost
model as the score, and a kernel sink as the world the moves land in.
Nothing in the engine or game layer is kernel-specific — a second
domain, not a second system (`notes/kernel-engineer-board.md`).

The claim is narrow, measured, and reproducible from the committed
tree:

> A schedule a kernel engineer writes — the pairwise-batched chunked
> scan over a concat-of-chunks spelling — was **reached by rewrite
> play on the extracted program, certified by derivation replay and
> verify-first numeric equality, and measured at or below the
> hand-written FLA reference implementation**, on a carrier the
> codegen domain could not even lower one arm earlier.

Two subsidiary claims carry it: every fused op the bank mints is
numerically equal to its spelled site on the sink's own runtime
(verify-first — a fused kernel ships on measurement, never on the
law's say-so), and a learned prior plays the board better than the
scripted line (0.560 vs 0.200 mean reward per episode, 24 held-out
cases, bit-identical reproduction under the leaderboard protocol;
`docs/results_kernel_check.md`).

The honest boundaries are named up front and expanded in
@sec-limitations: the schedule win is realised under CUDA-graph
replay (the eager scheduled path is Python-bound), the FLA number is
a carried retro from the parent repo (`fla-core` is absent here),
the comparison is parity on a launch-bound term rather than a win in
the GEMM-bound regime, and one fusion family — the decayed matmul —
verifies and prices but never pays at any measured size.

The repository is `handl-lang/kernelopt` (private); every number
below cites the artifact that produced it (@sec-repro).

# The substrate, briefly {#sec-substrate}

The platform paper carries this section [@mlopt-platform]; the short
version a reader needs here: a program is a term over a typed op
vocabulary; equality saturation [@tate2009; @willsey2021egg] closes
it under a law bank — rewrite rules as *data* (an LHS/RHS pattern
pair plus guard hooks or a declarative `cond`/`dspec` spec) — and
extraction picks the cheapest member under a pluggable cost model.
A `Sink` port lowers the extraction into a backend and verifies the
lowered pair.  The `Board` protocol wraps that loop as an episode —
`observe`/`step`, actions are rule names, reward is cost improvement —
and `play` is a domain registry: a domain is data (a case generator,
a board factory, a feature spec, an optional `deliver` hook), not a
subclass.  What this paper adds is *domain data only*: the codegen
law bank (`mlopt_kernel.laws`), the launch-counted cost model
(`mlopt_kernel.cost`), the kernel sink and scheduled executor
(`mlopt_kernel.sink`, `mlopt_kernel.scan`), the board
(`mlopt_kernel.board`), the `kernel` domain plugin
(`mlopt_kernel.play`), and a baked prior
(`mlopt_kernel.weights`).  The discovery side of the same substrate —
machine-minted laws and the admission gauntlet — is the companion
paper's story [@mlopt-graphopt].

# The domain {#sec-domain}

## The board: one program, codegen laws, a priced oracle

`KernelBoard` (`src/mlopt_kernel/board.py`) wraps `SearchEnv` — the
per-episode e-graph — with a kernel referee and kernel economics.
The state a player observes is the observable a real compiler has:
the program's op vocabulary (`ops`), the rule names whose *checked*
LHS occurs in the program (`matches` — the pattern binds *and* the
guard passes, so a listed move can actually fire), a `Const`-leaf
flag (the reciprocal site's tell), step count, and current/baseline
cost.  Actions are the bank's rule names plus `stop` — ending
evaluation is a legal move, and a free one: firing a codegen law
models a compile/measure oracle call, so each fire pays
`step_cost = 0.05` off its normalized `kernel_cost` improvement
while `stop` pays nothing.  "Is compiling this candidate worth the
oracle call" is the stop problem the board actually scores.  The
episode ends at the horizon (8), on `stop`, or when patience
exhausts; the terminal report carries the certificate verdict.

## The move set: twenty-six laws in three families

`KERNEL_RULES` (`src/mlopt_kernel/laws.py`) is twenty-six rules,
ordered so deeper fusions sit ahead of strength reductions:

| family | laws | what it mints |
|---|---|---|
| fusion folds | 19 | `FUSED_KERNEL_OPS` — `kf_*` compiled composites + `om_decayed` |
| schedule folds | 5 (`kern_fuse_chunk_scan_{2..6}`) | `om_chunk_scan` — a `SCHEDULED_KERNEL_OPS` marker |
| strength reductions | 2 | `mul`/`rsqrt`-free arithmetic the device emits anyway |

: The codegen bank, by family. {#tbl-bank}

The fusion arm mirrors what Inductor actually emits — elementwise
gate fusions (`a·σ(b)` → `kf_silu`, `a/(|b|+c)` → `kf_softsign`),
the exp/sum normalization a softmax really is (`kf_softmax` — the
kernel twin of the shipped `softmax_fold`), the norm blocks
(`kf_layernorm`, `kf_rmsnorm`), matmul epilogues (`kf_mm_bias`,
`kf_mm_scale`, `kf_mm_sb`, `kf_mm_gelu`), the attention chains
(`kf_softmax_mm`, and `kf_sdpa` folding the whole
`softmax(mm·s)·v` block — plain or `tanh` soft-capped — to one
launch), plus the second-generation residue family the measured
triton gap named: `kf_addmul_tanh` and `kf_silu_sigmoid` fold the
pointwise op a first-generation fusion *left surviving*, and
`kf_addmul2`/`kf_mul3` close the residue shapes the strength
reductions expose.  Side conditions are data where the `cond`/`dspec`
DSL reaches (the keepdim/single-axis gate on the softmax site is the
shipped `softmax_fold`'s verbatim); the chunk-scan family's `check`
runs the real plan parse — a concat that fails the parse keeps its
spelled evaluation, so the marker is never minted on a non-scan.

The scheduled family is the newest arm and the paper's headline
mechanism: `concat(x₁..xₙ, dim) → om_chunk_scan(x₁..xₙ, dim)` marks a
concat-of-chunks site as *one scheduled block* — a schedule boundary,
not a compiled composite.  Concat is variadic in the IR while a
pattern is fixed-arity, so the law is a family (the binary member
does the work on the extracted carrier's nested-binary spine: each
minted marker flattens again at the level above until the spine is
marked).

Two design notes the e-graph forces.  A *wrapper* marker
(`k_fused(X)`) would merge into `X`'s e-class and point back at it —
a cyclic enode the extractor can never pick — so fused ops take the
region's *leaves* as children and extraction chooses spelled-vs-fused
purely on cost.  And the bank deliberately stays out of the shipped
`DEFAULT` ruleset: these rules only pay under `kernel_cost`, so
`Optimizer.search`/`lower` never sees them — the codegen arm reaches
programs only through this domain's sink.

## The cost model: launches plus op weight

`kernel_cost` (`src/mlopt_kernel/cost.py`) prices two things: a
*launch* per emitted kernel and an *op weight* for the expensive
elementary ops (`pow` 4, `div`/`rsqrt`/`tanh`/`sigmoid`/`exp`/`gelu`
2 — the arithmetic a device kernel replaces anyway).  Fused ops
weigh exactly one launch.  Layout ops — `split`/`select`/`reshape`-family/`contiguous`/`detach_` —
price at zero (metadata-only on device); `concat` deliberately stays
a launch because `cat` materialises a copy.  `om_chunk_scan` prices
at *zero launches*: the marker emits no kernel of its own — the
block's GEMMs are billed at its arm operands — so a marked concat
spine strictly wins per node and the nested fold extracts whole
rather than piecemeal.  @sec-limitations names where this model is
honestly wrong.

## The sink and the scheduled executor

`KernelSink` (`src/mlopt_kernel/sink.py`) implements the `Sink` port
over a torch composite — a peer of the ONNX sink, smaller.  The
binding table covers the elementwise + reduction surface the bank
reaches, the layout ops real carriers carry, the `linear` GEMM slot,
and the decayed-scan vocabulary (`decay`/`decay_vec`/`om_decayed` —
carrier semantics vendored so the package stays carrier-free).
Each `FUSED_KERNEL_OPS` node lowers to `torch.compile` of its
composite body — one Inductor-generated kernel (Triton on CUDA) where
the spelled program dispatched an op at a time.  Each
`SCHEDULED_KERNEL_OPS` node routes to a cached `ScanRunner` — the
pairwise-batched chunk schedule vendored carrier-free into
`mlopt_kernel.scan`: batched score/state/pair GEMMs plus segment-sum
accumulation, slice restacks as reshape+permute views (zero kernels
where the spelled tape copied), per-forward and static-subtree memos
(the carrier's own memoised-eval choices).  A scheduled node whose
arms no longer parse falls back to the spelled `cat` — a drop-in,
never a silent drop.

# The referee {#sec-referee}

A codegen move scores only through three legs, in order of
cheapness:

1. **Derivation.**  The terminal extraction must certify: either the
   in-graph certificate replay (`EGraph.certificate` +
   `verify_certificate` — no discovery dependency) or, under the
   `kernel` play domain, `mlopt_discovery.verifier.verify_law`
   deriving the scheduled candidate against the spelled source under
   the bank.
2. **Numeric verify — verify-first.**  `KernelSink.verify` runs the
   spelled reference and the scheduled candidate *in this sink's own
   runtime* on random fp64 feeds.  Every fused op in the binding
   table verifies `max_abs = 0.0` against its spelled site; the
   extracted retnet carrier verifies `rel 1.6–1.9e-07` at fp32.
   A fused kernel ships on the report, never on the law.
3. **Measured pay.**  `bench.discovery.kernel` lowers both arms,
   verifies them, then times spelled vs scheduled (CUDA fp32,
   ~50-rep median) — plus a hand-Triton arm where a builder is
   registered (`bench/limits/triton`): the practitioner's kernel is
   the field baseline, and `kernel_flat` honestly reports `no triton
   kernel registered` rather than scoring a phantom win.

One measured finding belongs to the referee itself: the first
`kernel_softmax_mm` draft *failed* verify — not a law bug but the
spelled reference's `exp(qk)` overflowing fp32 where the fused
max-shifted softmax stays finite (`notes/kernel-engineer-board.md`).
The fused op is strictly more numerically stable than the spelling it
folds; the verify leg is what surfaced it.

# The players {#sec-players}

The `kernel` domain seats the shipped roster through the registry
seam — `linear`/`linear-greedy`/`linear-cold`/`random`/`playbook`
all play `kernel`; `distilled` and `neural` honestly report
does-not-play (their artifacts bind other boards).  The feature spec
(`KERNEL_SPEC`) is the observable the board exposes: progress and
banked improvement (`st:steps`, `st:improve`), the site count
(`st:sites`), binary op-presence flags (`st:op:*`), the match
interaction `x:m` (does this law's checked pattern occur here — the
feature that says a matching fusion is the one that can pay its
compile cost), the stop pair (`x:stop`, `x:stop:imp`), and hashed
rule buckets `a:r:*`.  The prior (`KERNEL_PLAYER_WEIGHTS`, v2) is
match-oracle imitation + REINFORCE, baked by
`scripts/train_kernel_prior.py`.

The leaderboard under the audited protocol — 24 held-out cases,
budget 8, `bench.players.run --boards kernel`, independent
reproduction bit-identical (`docs/results_kernel_check.md` §2):

| player | reward/ep | evals/ep | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `linear-greedy` | **0.5598** | 2.29 | short lines — extracts early |
| `linear` | 0.4992 | 3.42 | |
| `playbook` | 0.2004 | 8.0 | drains the budget |
| `linear-cold` | 0.1452 | 6.17 | the untrained control |
| `random` | 0.0993 | 5.63 | the floor |

: Kernel-board leaderboard — audited protocol, verified bit-identical.
{#tbl-leaderboard}

All 24 episodes end in certified extraction for every arm.  On the
grown bank + enlarged case pool the v2 prior re-measures higher
(`linear-greedy` 0.652, `linear` 0.587, `playbook` 0.290,
`linear-cold` −0.097, `random` −0.034 — same protocol, fresh pool;
`notes/kernel-engineer-board.md`), and the retrain is parity
held-out: 0.646 trained-greedy = 0.646 shipped-greedy — the v1
prior's generalization rode `x:m` alone, so v2 is honest provenance
(every rule's `a:r` bucket trained), not a gain.  The imitation
dependence does not shrink: cold-start REINFORCE plateaus at ~0.29
greedy — the imitation phase remains what carries the prior, kept as
a standing caveat.

# Results {#sec-results}

## Verified fusions against the spelled baseline {#sec-fusions}

The audited table — `python -m bench.discovery.kernel`, CUDA fp32,
50-rep median, the 11-case suite independently re-measured on the
same box (`docs/results_kernel_check.md` §1; every row
`verified=True` on both the scheduled and Triton arms):

| case | spelled µs | scheduled µs | speedup | triton µs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| kernel_silu | 475.0 | 209.6 | 2.27× | 201.5 |
| kernel_softsign | 666.2 | 211.7 | 3.15× | 201.3 |
| kernel_fma | 757.3 | 565.7 | 1.34× | 292.3 |
| kernel_swiglu | 754.3 | 303.0 | 2.49× | 291.6 |
| kernel_softmax | 667.0 | 210.0 | 3.18× | 199.5 |
| kernel_layernorm | 1050.5 | 210.5 | 4.99× | 200.1 |
| kernel_mm_bias | 856.6 | 763.2 | 1.12× | 940.9 |
| kernel_mm_scale_bias | 1088.5 | 850.9 | 1.28× | 920.7 |
| kernel_strength | 681.0 | 663.4 | 1.03× | 291.8 |
| kernel_mixed | 948.7 | 492.7 | 1.93× | 291.0 |
| kernel_flat (control) | 662.4 | 663.2 | 0.999× | — skip |

: The 11-case audit table — verified fusions, hand-Triton baseline.
{#tbl-fusion}

The table is honest in both directions.  Single fusions land *at*
the hand kernel (209–212 µs vs 199–202) — a compiled `kf_*`
composite matches a tutorial-tile Triton kernel on the cases the law
folds whole.  The mm-epilogue rows invert the comparison the other
way: Inductor's mm path (763/851) *beats* the tutorial tile
(941/921) at this size.  And the partial-fusion rows show the
residue the next arm was built for: `fma` 566 vs 292, `mixed` 493
vs 291, `strength` 663 vs 292 — the folded region pays, the leftover
pointwise launch does not.

The bank then grew to 21 laws over three more measured arms
(`notes/kernel-engineer-board.md`; the case suite is now 29).  The
residue rows closed — `kernel_fma` 566→~309 µs (≈/beats triton),
`kernel_mixed` 493→308, `kernel_strength` 663→369 (7→1 launches,
1.88×, ~90% of the hand kernel's 333) — the whole attention block
folded to `kf_sdpa` (1.78×; soft-capped twin 1.92×, *beating* the
hand pipeline it trailed as a two-launch chain), and the
pointwise-pair folds paid (addmul2 2.44×, powscale 1.61×).  The arms'
honest negatives are in @sec-limitations: the two bias-free mm
epilogues measure parity/loss (mm_scale 1.01×, mm_gelu 0.94×), and
every `om_decayed` family case measures 0.74–0.99×.

## Case study: the retnet carrier {#sec-casestudy}

The domain's real target is not the bench archetypes — it is the
~1.6× residual the parent's whole-model audit left between the best
delivered chunked-decayed carrier (`fused32+graph` 0.454 ms) and the
FLA reference (~0.28 ms, carried retro).  The independent check
(`docs/results_kernel_check.md` §4) found the kernel board
structurally unable to touch it on three grounds: 8 of the
extracted carrier's 14 ops were outside `KernelSink.supported_ops`
(unlowerable at all); of the bank, only `kern_div_recip` fired on
the term (cost 368→349, still unlowerable); and the bank sits
outside `DEFAULT`, so the delivery path never sees it.  Two arms
closed the gap; the measured ladder is the paper's headline.

**Arm 1 — vocabulary** (`docs/results_kernel_vocab.md`).  Nine
binding-table entries (`linear`, `concat`, `split`,
`contiguous`/`detach`/`detach_`, `decay`/`decay_vec`, `om_decayed`)
plus `kern_fuse_om_decayed` folding the spelled `matmul(mul(s,d),v)`
site — the op keeps the carrier name, so an extracted `om_decayed`
enode and a minted one are the same kernel.  The extracted carrier
(T=512/K=4, root `concat`, 14 distinct ops, 145 nodes) now lowers
with **0/14 ops outside the table** and verifies (`rel 1.61e-07`,
fp32).  But the speed gap was *schedule, not vocabulary*: the
sink's per-op dispatch tape under a CUDA graph lands 1.011 ms vs
the "batched" carrier's 0.537 ms — replayed per-op launches cost
~2× the pairwise-batched chunk schedule.  Compiled per-op fused ops
are *slower* than eager at this tape length (5.49 vs 4.29 ms —
dispatch premium beats the fusion win at 145 nodes), and whole-graph
`torch.compile` of the executor graph-breaks into fragments
(3.81 ms).

**Arm 2 — schedule** (`docs/results_chunk_scan.md`).  The
`kern_fuse_chunk_scan` family marks the concat spine; the executor
gains scheduled dispatch plus a per-forward memo (a DAG-shared
subterm — the shared q/k/v projections feeding every chunk's
`split` — evaluates once per call, not once per use; that memo
alone moves the spelled tape+graph 1.011 → 0.537 ms).  On the real
extraction — a nested-binary concat over 7 chunk arms of *mixed*
size (4×32 + 3×128) — the fold mints `om_chunk_scan` at 5 of 6
concat nodes (`kernel_cost` 206 → 201); the root concat stays
spelled because the uniform-shape gate vetoes the mixed group — the
same gate the carrier's own `ChunkedDecayModule` has.

| arm | med ms | note |
|---|---|---|
| spelled-eager32 | 0.396 | one unchunked masked mm |
| fused(exec)32 | 2.634 | incumbent per-op executor, eager |
| kernel_tape (per-op, eager) | 3.012 | memo'd (was 4.29) |
| kernel_scan (scheduled, eager) | 2.154 | batched plan, Python-dispatched |
| kernel_scan (spelled-cat path) | 2.262 | `compile_fused=False` fallback |
| kernel_tape + CUDA graph | 0.537 | was 1.011 — the memo alone |
| carrier32 + CUDA graph | 0.538 | **serial fallback** — see text |
| fused32 + CUDA graph (incumbent) | 0.454 | the audit's delivery path |
| **kernel_scan + CUDA graph** | **0.271** | two scheduled blocks + one cat |
| fla-chunk | ~0.28 | carried retro — `fla-core` absent |

: The chunked-scan ladder — fp32 CUDA, median of 30; verify32
`rel 1.93e-07`, passed. {#tbl-ladder}

The ladder is honest in both directions, and one cell needs the
text: the "batched carrier" arm at 0.537 turns out to be **serial**
— `build_decayed_plan` returns `False` on this exact term (the
mixed 32/128 chunk sizes fail its uniform-shape gate), so the 0.537
was the serial IRModule under a graph all along; the memo'd tape
reaching the same 0.537 confirms they are the same schedule.  The
pairwise-batched carrier never ran on this term — `om_chunk_scan`
is the *first* lowering that actually batches it (per uniform-chunk
group).  Net: the scheduled fold at **0.271 ms beats every arm** —
the carrier (0.537), the incumbent fused delivery (0.454), the
spelled eager module (0.396) — and lands at or below the ~0.28 ms
FLA reference.  The named residual is attacked; what the claim does
*not* say is in @sec-limitations.

# Limitations and honest negatives {#sec-limitations}

- **The eager scheduled path is Python-bound.**  The schedule win is
  realised under graph replay: `kernel_scan` eager measures 2.15 ms
  vs 0.271 ms graphed — the batched plan replays at Python dispatch
  cost.  The small bench row `kernel_chunk_scan` honestly reports
  0.198× (Python-bound at toy sizes, same signature as
  `kernel_decayed_intra`'s 0.546×).  Making the plan tape
  compile-friendly is unexplored — the runner is a term-walking
  evaluator, not a compilable composite.
- **The remaining `cat`.**  Mixed chunk sizes stay split: the fold
  minted 5 of 6 concat nodes; the root survives as one spelled `cat`
  of two scheduled blocks — measured headroom ~1 launch.  A
  whole-scan fold needs per-group plans under one marker.
- **The FLA comparison is parity on a launch-bound term.**  At
  T=512/d=16 the scheduled block still emits ~10 kernels; the real
  FLA kernel does the scan in-register and would pull away in the
  GEMM-bound regime at larger T/K.  The honest next arm is a fused
  Triton scan in `bench/limits/triton/` style — not built.  And
  `fla-core` is absent here: the ~0.28 ms reference is a carried
  retro number from the parent repo, not a re-measurement.
- **`om_decayed` is a vocabulary win, not a codegen win.**  The fold
  verifies and prices 1 launch, but measures 0.74–0.90× at bench
  sizes and a monotone 0.97→0.99 asymptote across the T=512–4096
  ladder — never paying at any measured size.  The deficit is the
  per-op `torch.compile` dispatch premium (~30–600 µs) against a
  saved materialisation that is bandwidth-trivial next to a real
  GEMM: the launch-counting cost model over-prices this fold.  It
  earns its place by letting the bank *name* the decayed element —
  and as the intra site the chunk-scan parser accepts — not by its
  measured pay.
- **The launch model's other misses.**  `concat` priced at 1 launch
  is a deliberate approximation; two mm-epilogue folds measure
  parity/loss (mm_scale 1.01×, mm_gelu 0.94× — mm-dominated, the
  absorbed pointwise is noise at this size); bench variance moved
  `kernel_decayed_chunks` from 2.35× to ~parity across re-runs
  (recompile-limit churn — variance-dominated, documented).
- **Compile economics invert at tape length.**  Per-op compiled
  fused ops lose to their eager bodies on a 145-node tape (5.49 vs
  4.29 ms); whole-graph `torch.compile` of the executor graph-breaks
  per binding call (3.81 ms).  The `kf_*` pay is a bench-case result
  (one fused op per program), not a long-tape result.
- **Bank outside `DEFAULT`.**  The codegen laws pay only under
  `kernel_cost`, so they are deliberately out of the shipped
  ruleset — `Optimizer.search`/`lower` never fires them; the reach
  runs through this domain's board + sink.
- **The prior rides imitation.**  Cold-start REINFORCE plateaus
  (~0.29 greedy) while the warm-started prior holds 0.65; what
  carries cold-start exploration is unmeasured.  The bank has since
  grown past the v2 prior's trained buckets — a v3 retrain is the
  open arm.
- **Private evidence.**  The box (RTX 2050 / 11 GB), the noise band
  (load average 5–7 during the audit), and the numbers are
  repo-internal.  `kernel_decayed`'s per-run spread (0.69–1.17×)
  is the honest statement: small-case dispatch rows are
  variance-dominated.

# Related work {#sec-related}

**Schedule languages.**  Halide [@ragan2013halide] is the ancestor
of the split this paper exploits — the algorithm is the term, the
schedule is a second object — but Halide schedules are hand-chosen
or autotuned over a fixed body, where `om_chunk_scan` is a schedule
*minted by a verified rewrite*: the schedule boundary enters the
program as a law-applied term, checked by the same certificate
machinery as a fusion.  Triton [@tillet2019triton] is the
practitioner's language and our field baseline — every `triton µs`
column above is a hand kernel in `bench/limits/triton/`; the
scheduled fold is what the tutorial tile does not express.

**Learned autotuning.**  TVM [@chen2018tvm], AutoTVM
[@chen2018autotvm] and Ansor [@zheng2020ansor] learn a cost model
over a *template* space — the program's semantics are fixed by the
template and the search prices parameter settings.  kernelopt's
moves are semantic rewrites instead: the search changes *what the
program is*, and the referee must re-prove equality because the
moved program is a different object, not a re-parameterized one.
The analogue of their learned cost model is the player prior over
certified moves.

**Inductor as incumbent.**  PyTorch 2 / Inductor
[@ansel2024pytorch2] fuses pointwise ops and emits the graph a
human optimizer could reach — our fused ops literally ride it (a
`kf_*` lowers to `torch.compile` of its composite).  The measured
difference is the schedule boundary: on the 145-node carrier
Inductor sees a per-op tape or graph-breaks on the evaluator
(3.81 ms), where the marked concat folds to a batched plan
(0.271 ms).  The contribution is not a better Inductor but a
verified route to a schedule it cannot name.

**Rewrite-level prior art.**  TENSAT [@yang2021tensat] applies
equality saturation to tensor graphs with fixed, hand-written rule
sets; TASO [@jia2019taso] auto-generates and formally verifies
graph substitutions; Glenside [@smith2021glenside] rediscovers
access-pattern rewrites.  kernelopt's bank is the same object class
as theirs — fixed, hand-written laws — so the differentiation here
is not the bank's provenance but the *game*: the laws are moves a
learned player sequences under a measured referee, on a board whose
domain grew under the player (the chunk-scan arm did not exist when
the v1 prior shipped, and the prior generalizes to it untrained via
`x:m`).

**Learned play over compilation.**  CompilerGym
[@cummins2022compilergym] casts optimization as RL over a fixed
action space; AlphaTensor [@fawzi2022alphatensor] searches one
fixed structure for faster algorithms.  The kernel board is the
same shape over a *verified* move set — the certified referee is
the piece those environments approximate with a cost model alone.

**The FLA reference.**  The `fla-chunk` row is the
flash-linear-attention library's [@fla] chunked linear-attention
kernel — the hand-written in-register scan the honest residual
names as the real comparison at scale.

# Reproduction {#sec-repro}

All numbers are reproducible from the committed tree at
`handl-lang/kernelopt` (private):

```sh
uv sync
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q                    # the unit layer (law guards, verify-first sink)
.venv/bin/python -m bench.discovery.kernel            # the measured case suite
.venv/bin/python -m mlopt_kernel.play --domain kernel \
    --train-cases 8 --eval-cases 4 --budget 8         # the game
.venv/bin/python -m mlopt_kernel.play --domain kernel --deliver
```

The evidence docs each claim cites are `docs/results_kernel_check.md`
(the independent audit: 11-case table, leaderboard, the unlowerable
verdict), `docs/results_kernel_vocab.md` (the vocabulary arm and the
tape ladder — probes `bench/drivers/probes/kernel_vocab_probe.py`)
and `docs/results_chunk_scan.md` (the schedule arm and the headline
ladder — probe `bench/drivers/probes/kernel_scan_probe.py`, run in
the parent env with `PYTHONPATH=<kernelopt>/src`); the design note
with the grown-bank measured arms is
`notes/kernel-engineer-board.md`.  The retnet carrier extraction is
the parent repo's (`handl-lang/graphopt`, `mlopt_carriers`
`decayed_lower`); FLA is the carried retro there.
